Subject: Kickoff: Evaluation plan & contracting owners for AcmeRx pilot

Hi Kelly —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As discussed, I wanted to get a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) started so we can align owners, milestones, and expected close timelines for the pilot evaluation. I’ve attached a lightweight MAP template to this thread (Redwood_MAP_Template_v1.xlsx) — feel free to edit directly or we can iterate.

High-level proposed milestones (suggested spans):
- Week 0–1: Kickoff + environment access & sample dataset exchange
- Week 2: Technical evaluation (integration + latency/throughput checks)
- Week 3: Security & privacy review (questionnaire + evidence)
- Week 4: Commercial review (T&Cs, PO + pricing sign-off)
- Week 5: Pilot launch / handoff to CS

Key asks:
1) Please confirm the primary procurement and legal contacts on your side so we can route contract drafts and redlines to the right people.
2) Are there any hard-compliance milestones or internal blackout dates we should avoid?
3) Would you prefer a single SOW + terms or staged SOWs per pilot phase?

Proposed next step: 30-minute kickoff on Wednesday (Feb 25) to walk through the MAP and assign owners. I’ve tentatively suggested times in a separate calendar invite.

I’ve looped in Marissa (solutions) to own the evaluation plan and Karthik (contracts) to handle redline/DocuSign logistics from our side.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_Template_v1.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

—

Hi Kelly / Tom / Jill —

Pleasure to meet you virtually. I’m the contracts lead at Redwood and will coordinate our review and execution workflow. To set expectations on process/timing:

- Drafts: We’ll share a clean SOW + our standard terms within 24-48 hours (I’ve attached a clean SOW for reference).
- Redlines: Please send redlines back as PDF comments or via DocuSign comments; we’ll aim to respond within 5 business days for a first pass.
- Negotiation window: For pilot agreements we try to limit substantive negotiation to 2 rounds to keep timelines predictable.
- Execution: We prefer DocuSign for signatures; if you need alternate execution (paper PO + signature), flag it early so we can coordinate finance.

If there are any specific procurement clauses (payment terms, indemnity caps, data processing addenda) you expect to change, call them out now so we can surface early with our finance and security teams.

I’ve attached: Redwood_Standard_Terms_v3.pdf and a draft SOW named Redwood_Pilot_SOW_AcmeRx.docx.

—

Soojin / Karthik —

Thanks for the materials and the proposed timeline. Procurement is generally aligned with the flow you outlined, with two notes from our side:

1) PO timing: internal PO approvals typically take ~10 business days once terms are agreed and finance receives the invoice. We can try to accelerate, but please assume ~2 weeks for PO issuance.
2) Payment terms: our standard is Net-30; if Redwood requires a different cadence, let me know so I can route approvals.

I attached our procurement requirements for the vendor checklist. Regarding the redline process: the 5-business-day response window sounds fair. We’ll have Jill review the first draft and return comments.
